chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, who said:
I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام that some people say: the inner part of the two ears is part of the face, and their outer part is part of the head,
So he said: There is neither washing upon them nor wiping.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Yūnus, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, “Are the two ears part of the head?” He said: “Yes.” I said: “Then when I wipe my head, do I wipe my ears?” He said: “Yes. It is as though I am looking at my father, with a fold on his neck, and he used to clip his head closely when he cut it; it is as though I am looking while the water runs down upon his neck,”

then it is to be understood as being upon taqiyyah, because it agrees with the doctrines of the ʿāmmah and conflicts with the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, as we have explained in Kitāb Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation/precautionary conformity, invoked here to explain the conflicting report
key_terms.الرَّأْسِ: the head, the area wiped in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْأُذُنَيْنِ: the two ears, discussed here in relation to wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْقُرْآنِ: the Qur'an, whose apparent meaning is cited as the basis for preferring one ruling
key_terms.الْوَجْهِ: the face, one of the areas washed in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.غَسْلٌ: washing, as a ritual act in purification

ai.seo_question: Are the ears washed or wiped in wudu (ablution) according to this hadith from al-Istibṣār?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of the ears in wudu (ablution), stating that they are not subject to independent washing or wiping. A second report that appears to support wiping the ears is presented, then reconciled by stating that it was issued in taqiyyah because it accords with the view of the ʿāmmah and opposes the apparent meaning of the Qur'an.
